lessons.rule:
Main-hand levels are the second engine (+6 levels is about +1.3 blinds).
- Choose the main hand by how often you can draw it with 2 discards: you should be able to draw it in 3 of 4 hands. How often you have played it so far does not matter, unless you own Telescope (its pack planet is for your most played hand).
- Pair is the default. It is always drawable, and Sly, Jolly, Duo and Mercury support it. Leave Pair only for a real signal (Spare Trousers, Mad or Clever already owned, a steady planet supply). One off-plan planet from a pack is not a signal.
- Use Full House, Straight or Flush only with a real enabler.
- Commit by the end of ante 1-2, and make sure the round player actually plays that hand. Do not let a joker (e.g. Runner) pull plays toward Straights, or spread plays over Full House, Two Pair and High Card. If the jokers you own really support a different hand, commit to that hand by ante 3.
- Take every planet for the main hand (Mercury whenever it is offered). Skip off-plan planets even when they are free.
- Targets: level 2-3 by the ante 2 boss (buy at least one main-hand planet before it), 3-5 by antes 3-4, 6-9 by antes 5-6.
- While below target: buy the main-hand planet on sight ($3-4). Buy it before any joker reroll, and always before a 2nd reroll in the same shop. Below level 3 at ante 3 or below level 4 at ante 4, planets also come before holding interest above $25. Take Meteor Tags.
- Celestial packs: buy the planet directly when the shop sells it. Otherwise open a Celestial pack while below target if you keep about $10-15 after it (more freely once $25 is covered). Prefer it to rerolls, $6+ flat jokers and slow scalers, because a level is certain score and a reroll is just as much a gamble. Do not pass packs because 'Mercury is only 25%'. Never open one that leaves you unable to fix the coming blind.
- If the main hand's planets still have not shown up by ante 3, consider moving to a drawable hand whose planets you keep being offered.
- Value Telescope and Planet Merchant highly.

In antes 1-2, survival beats interest until the board has 2 lasting, unconditional scoring jokers (+Mult or chips that fire on ordinary hands) and the main hand is level 2 or higher. Survival means the current ante's blinds. When the current blind already reads 95%+, do not pay for perishable or off-plan jokers, packs or rerolls. Until those 2 scorers are in place:
- Do not leave a shop holding $15+ while a blind is failing. Spend down to about $10, and in ante 1 go below $10 only if the next blind would fail.
- Cheap +Mult stopgaps (Jolly, Raised Fist, Gros Michel, or any joker with a perishable sticker) is a bridge only when the current blind fails without it. Otherwise take a non-perishable scorer even if it is slightly weaker. Never let two stopgaps expire in the same ante or right at a boss.
- Use the Yellow Deck head start on Buffoon packs only as part of a plan to reach $25 by ante 3. In ante 1, open one only if you could still afford a shop joker or a reroll after a miss. If the pack misses, the next shop is a forced search for a scorer, not a place to save.
- Every joker slot and pack pick goes to scoring. Do not take utility or economy jokers (Drunkard, Chaos, Splash, Mail-In Rebate, To the Moon, Cloud 9, Certificate) or a $10 voucher like Grabber.
- Zero scoring jokers before any blind from the ante 1 Big Blind on is an emergency. Buy any affordable scorer. If there is none, do one $5 reroll, then open an Arcana pack (Judgement). Never enter a blind with an empty board while holding $10+.
- With no scoring jokers, play the highest base hand you can draw (Flush, Straight, Three of a Kind, then Two Pair) and take pack jokers that pay off now (Runner over Certificate).
- An early xMult (e.g. Card Sharp) must be followed at once by an unconditional base joker and a main-hand planet.
- Take a value generator only when the next boss is safe by the conservative check.
Once the 2 lasting scorers are in place, bank: aim for $25 by the end of ante 2, and hold $25 from ante 3.

Reroll limits:
- At most 2 rerolls per shop, and only 1 in an ante the outlook shows as safe. Spread them across shops. Never chain escalating rerolls ($5, $6, $7, $8) in one shop. Pay for a joker on offer rather than for more looks at the shop.
- Ante 1: do not reroll or spend below about $10 unless the next blind would fail. With a safe blind, do not reroll below $20. The only exception is the single emergency reroll when the board is empty before a blind; never chain a second one. Leave ante 1 with $10-15 so the ante 2 shops can buy two scorers.
- In antes 1-2, never spend $15+ rerolling one shop.
- In a safe ante, do not reroll if it drops you below the next $5 interest tier.
- Never reroll below $20 unless the NEXT blind reads below 70%. A bad forecast 1-2 antes out is a reason to keep interest and buy planets, not to empty the bank on rerolls.
- With a joker that scales with money held (Bull, Bootstraps), check the next-blind outlook after each spend. Stop if it would fall below about 85% or drop more than 5 points. Spending that breaks the next blind while chasing a later one is not survival.
- From ante 3, reroll only with money above $25 ($28 with a rental), and only if you can open a slot: know which joker you would sell before you reroll.
- Stop once one shop has used about $20 on rerolls. Never pay $8-10 for a reroll unless you hold $60+.
Never rerolling at all is also a failure. While the board has fewer than 2 multipliers, use 1-2 $5 rerolls per shop with money above the floor, in the early shops of the ante rather than the boss shop. If the boss itself is the problem, first look for a fix aimed at that boss (Director's Cut, glass from Justice, a skip that avoids it).

Rentals and debt.
Ante 1: buy no rentals, even at $1, unless the current blind fails without one. Exception: if you hold an xMult with no base, a big flat-chips rental (Stuntman +250) or an affordable Bootstraps is worth it.
Antes 1-3: never buy a flat rental just to fix a single blind. Before ante 3, buy a rental only if it is a core scorer you would still want at ante 5. Count the $3 per round as part of its price, about $15-20 over the rest of a run.
xMult exception: from ante 2, if the board has no xMult and an upcoming boss reads below 50%, an affordable xMult with a rental sticker (even eternal + rental; e.g. Acrobat, Vampire, Card Sharp) beats any flat +Mult option. Refuse it only if you already carry a rental or it cannot fire for your hand.
From ante 2-3 on: one rental that is a lasting scorer and fits the main hand (Hanging Chad, a growing joker, Even Steven on an even-heavy deck) is a fine buy if you have a free slot and $28 banked.
Always:
- With a rental, the floor is $28, not $25. Never spend to $0 while holding one: the fee puts you into debt and locks you out of the next shops.
- Never use Credit Card or debt to pay for scoring in antes 1-3. At $0 or below, buy no rentals.
- Never take a perishable rental. Take an eternal rental only under the xMult exception. Never carry two rentals at once.
- Sell a survival rental before any other joker once a non-rental scorer can replace it, or once the next blind is 90%+ safe without it.
- Do not let the $28/$31 floor block buys that improve the build.
- Before a boss that costs money (e.g. The Tooth), enter with cash for the cards you expect to play + $3 per rental + $5.

Judge a board by its reliable scoring. The outlook is simulated with the boss's effect and the build as it is, but it still averages over lucky draws. When reaching the target depends on a conditional joker (suit, rank or hand-type jokers, Flower Pot, Idol, Ancient, Castle) or on unreliable pieces, treat the boss as less safe than shown. Do not trust a high outlook on an empty board: with zero jokers and every hand at level 1, treat any blind of 450 or more as below 80%, whatever the simulator says. Before each ante step (especially 3 to 4, which is x2.8), check that the next ante's Small Blind is not already below 70% in the outlook. If it is, keep buying lasting scoring even if it costs an interest tier.

Unreliable scoring is backup, not the plan. That includes perishable jokers, decaying ones (Ice Cream, Popcorn, Seltzer), random ones (Misprint), time-limited ones (Seltzer, 10 hands) and destroyable ones (Gros Michel, 1 in 6).
- Count a perishable as gone at its expiry, and start looking for a permanent replacement 2 rounds before.
- Never let two perishables expire in the same ante or right at a boss.
- Once the outlook flags a cliff 1-2 antes out, stop buying perishable stopgaps. Save for xMult and planets instead.
- Replace a shrinking chips joker before it falls to about half its value (Ice Cream below about 75 chips).
- From ante 3, treat a flat joker that scores under 10% of the hand as a slot to free. Sell it as soon as the shop offers anything better for the main hand.
- If more than half the board's scoring is unreliable, work out the bad case: Gros Michel gone, Misprint at about +5, decay after 4 more hands. Keep buying lasting scoring until the boss clears without those pieces.
- Never let a perishable or rental joker be your only chips source.

Interest against forecasts. When every blind in the current ante reads 90%+, do not reroll or buy speculative packs below $25 ($28 with a rental) because of a low reading for a boss 1-2 antes away. This applies in antes 1-3 too, once 2 lasting scorers exist. 'Survival first' covers only the current ante's blinds, or the next blind when it reads below 70%. A high outlook that rests on a variable joker (Ancient, Idol, Castle), or a boss that hides information, is no reason to spend the bank either.
Exception: when the outlook shows the next ante's Big Blind or Boss below about 20-30% (especially at ante 4 with no xMult), act in the current ante, not the dying one. Spend the surplus above $25 across the current ante's shops while rerolls still cost $5:
- main-hand planets and Celestial packs
- Arcana packs for glass or steel on trigger cards
- one $5 xMult reroll per shop
Do not save it for the first shop of the dying ante, and do not dump it into escalating rerolls in one shop.
When the boss is below 50% and you dip into survival money, judge each $ by how much it raises the boss estimate. Prefer a main-hand planet already in the shop, then joker rerolls or a tarot that edits trigger cards. If two buys in a row miss, stop and keep the interest.

From ante 2 to ante 5, while the board has fewer than 2 multiplier sources (a suit-dependent x1.5 such as Ancient counts as half), spend all surplus above $25 in every shop. Use 1-2 $5 rerolls spread across shops, Buffoon packs, and xMult or +Mult jokers. If the main hand is below its level target, buy its planet first.
- Never pass a real xMult (The Idol, Cavendish, Card Sharp, Acrobat and similar) just to keep an interest tier while a slot is open, or because of a rental or eternal sticker (see the rentals rule). Empty slots never grow.
- Do not swap one flat +Mult or chips joker for another as a fix. It only counts if the outlook rises.
- Joker Stencil is a stopgap: take any xMult, scaling or growing joker even if it lowers Stencil, and judge it by the score needed 1-2 antes ahead.
- Do not spend this surplus on Arcana, Spectral or Standard packs that add one-card tweaks, or on Golden Joker or other economy, unless you are aiming at a specific card the build needs.
- Spend a windfall of $20+ over target (Investment Tag, big interest) this way before the Small Blind, spread across that ante's shops.

Buy only jokers that fire on what you actually play and own.
- No jokers for a different hand type (Droll/Crafty for Flush, Crazy or Devious for Straight, Zany for Three of a Kind, Clever for Two Pair) as a bridge or as filler. Buy unconditional +Mult or chips instead (Abstract, Banner, Popcorn, or Jolly when Pair is the main hand; not Half Joker, which needs 3 or fewer cards, nor Blackboard, a conditional xMult that needs held Spades/Clubs), or reroll to find one.
- No jokers that need cards you lack (Stone Joker with no Stone cards). Early on, skip conditional support (Scary Face; Mime without a strong held-in-hand card).
- Early on, buy jokers that scale, multiply or add plain +Mult. If the shop has none, keep the money rather than filling slots.
- No sideways swaps. Do not sell a flat or conditional joker to buy another of the same kind. From ante 3, do not buy flat or perishable fillers (Swashbuckler) that only nudge a failing boss estimate, unless that joker alone lifts the next blind above about 80%. A swap must add a multiplier, a lasting chips source your deck triggers, or a scaler you will feed for several antes. Otherwise keep the slot and the money for an xMult or a main-hand planet.
- Do not hold scalers that pull against each other on discards. Banner and Green Joker want zero discards; Castle wants many. Pick one direction when you buy the second one, and sell or skip the one that conflicts.
- Do not play Straights or Flushes as filler without an enabler. In a desperate last shop, do not switch to a hand you can't reliably draw: with 8 cards, 2 discards and no Four Fingers or Shortcut, a Straight in one hand is only about a 25-30% event. The empty-board case is the exception: see the zero-joker rule.

Crisis cash discipline: when a blind or boss looks lost, every purchase must raise it clearly. That means about +15 points on the boss, or lifting a failing blind above about 50%. A buy that moves a doomed boss from 15% to 20% is not a fix; keep the money for the next shop and the next ante.
- When a boss you must beat is below 50%, spend at most about half your money on rerolls in one shop. Stop when the next reroll would leave under about $12 for the remaining shops before the boss. Each later shop is a fresh roll for xMult, and you need money there to buy the xMult plus a planet.
- While shops remain in the ante, never spend to $0. Keep at least the price of a common xMult ($6) plus $3 per rental due at round end.
- Grabber and other vouchers, random Arcana or Celestial packs, off-plan levels and sideways flat-joker swaps do not count as fixes. Never spend your last money on a voucher and then skip a blind.
- Flag the run as in trouble as soon as the outlook shows the next ante at 0-15%. React with targeted certain upgrades, not by emptying the bank in a panic.

Eternal jokers and slot flexibility:
- From ante 3, keep at least 2 joker slots that can be sold. Keep at most 2 Eternals that are not xMult. Never buy an Eternal flat +Mult or chips joker if that makes 3 or more locked slots, unless the next blind reads below 60% without it and no non-Eternal option does as well. Before any Eternal buy, ask: 'when the xMult shows up, which slot does it go in?'
- In antes 1-2, do not lock a slot with an Eternal joker that is flat filler or will be a weak flat effect by ante 4 (Eternal plain Joker, Splash, Sly, Arrowhead, Fibonacci). Take one only if the next blind is below 70% without it.
- When opening a Buffoon pack with no jokers, rank the choices by how many chips they add to an ordinary hand right now, and take a scorer if there is one. If the pack has no scorer and 4+ slots are free, an economy joker (even an Eternal one like Reserved Parking) still beats wasting the $4. Judge the locked slot by how many jokers you can realistically afford.
- Do not buy a Buffoon pack, or skip for a Buffoon Tag, when every slot is full and the only sellable joker is a key scorer. Decide before paying what you would sell; otherwise spend on a planet or keep the interest.

Do not skip blinds in an ante where the boss is below about 40-50%, or where the boss estimate is likely optimistic (xMult that depends on drawing specific ranks, or a boss that drains levels like The Arm). Play the last blind before the boss if it is at least 60%, and use that shop to fix the board. Rare, Uncommon, Voucher, Coupon and money tags (Economy, Handy, Investment) pay out only after a later blind, so skipping sends you into the next blind with the same board. When the run is struggling, skip only if the tag itself fixes the next blind. Skip the pre-boss blind for a money tag only if the boss has read at least 90% for two or more shops in a row and the shop you give up has nothing you want. A skip gives up the blind payout, the unused-hand money and a whole shop. When a Rare Tag's free joker appears, take it, selling a perishable or flat joker to make room.

Keep your xMult. Do not sell your only xMult joker (Card Sharp, a permanent x3 Flower Pot, etc.) for a flat or scaling +Mult joker unless the boss you are about to face is impossible with it. Before any swap that removes a multiplier, compare the next ante's outlook with and without the swap, not just the next blind's. $3 a round in rent for an x3 is cheap, and one reliable xMult is worth about +2.5 blinds. Conditional xMult like Flower Pot is still a bonus, not the engine. It checks only scoring cards, so a kicker never helps. Two Pair covers all four suits only about 1 time in 6, and Full House about half the time. Do not pick the main hand around it, and do not accept an outlook that depends on it firing. When it struggles against one boss, change how you play (five-card hands that cover all four suits, Wild cards) rather than selling it.

Score the build against the actual boss. Once the boss is shown, rate every shop of the ante against its rule, not against the Small or Big Blind. For a one-hand boss like The Needle, only per-hand +Mult, xMult and main-hand planets count. Skip delayed or counter jokers (Loyalty Card, Ride the Bus, Runner, Wee, Lucky Cat) and economy until the one-hand score clears. A boss debuff (e.g. The Goad on Spades) applies only to the boss, so play normally in the Small and Big Blinds. In any round rated below about 95%, turn off grow_joker style goals and play the highest score each hand. Grow scalers only on blinds that are about 100% safe. Do not buy fresh slow scalers (Square, Wee, Runner) at ante 3+ unless they can be fed for free.

Before buying any scoring joker, compare the board's typical chips and Mult on the main hand, and buy for the smaller one. Once Mult is above about 30 and chips are under about 100, another +Mult joker is nearly worthless. Buy chips instead (main-hand planets, Stuntman, Hiker, Blue Joker, Square, Ice Cream, Bull) or xMult, and skip flat +Mult even when it is free.
